items.text: Roberta Flack's "Killing Me Softly with His Song" was the longest-running number one on the Billboard Hot 100 in 1973, with five weeks at the top.
items.question: Where were you living when Roberta Flack's "Killing Me Softly with His Song" was on the radio, and who in your house had the record?
source_quote: The Billboard Hot 100 is a chart published since August 1958 by Billboard magazine which ranks the best-performing singles in the United States. In 1973, it was compiled based on a combination of sales and airplay data sourced from surveys of retail outlets and playlists submitted by radio stations respectively. During the year, 27 different singles spent time at number one, the most since 1966.
The year's longest-running number one was Roberta Flack's "Killing Me Softly with His Song", with five non-consecutive weeks in the top spot.

items.text: On June 9, 1973, Secretariat won the Belmont Stakes by 31 lengths and became a Triple Crown winner, the first since 1948.
items.question: Where were you when Secretariat won the Belmont Stakes, and who did you watch the race with?
items.source_quote: June 9 – Secretariat wins the Belmont Stakes by 31 lengths becoming a Triple Crown winner and breaking a 25-year hiatus since 1948.

items.text: Skylab, the United States' first space station, was launched on May 14, 1973.

items.source_quote: May 14 – Skylab, the United States' first space station, is launched.
